svg.title: The uniform maximum stays skewed and beats the regular rate
svg.desc: Left panel: the rescaled distance from theta to the sample maximum has almost the same right-skewed exponential shape at sample sizes five, twenty and two hundred. Right panel: its standard deviation falls far faster than the rate a regular model allows.
svg.text: Uniform(0, theta): a different limit and a different rate
t, in units of theta over n
Density of n times theta minus the maximum
n = 5 orange, n = 20 blue, n = 200 purple
the three lie almost on top of it
the density is largest at zero
and falls away. No bell shape
Standard deviation, in units of theta
would force, one over root n
the root of n times n plus two
Regularity failed, so neither the floor nor the normal limit applies, and what replaces them is not a weaker version of either.
The limit shape is one-sided rather than symmetric, and the rate improves from one over root n to one over n.
At n = 12 the marked standard deviations are 0.289 and 0.077, a factor of 3.74 below the floor a careless calculation reports.
